did_you_know.text: Did you know? David organized the army into twelve monthly divisions. A different division served each month, and each division had 24,000 men.
Did you know? Jashobeam son of Zabdiel, one of the descendants of Perez, is listed as the chief of the army officers for the first month.
Did you know? Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the division for the third month, and the text also describes him as a mighty warrior among the Thirty.
Did you know? Heldai the Netophathite commanded the division for the twelfth month, bringing the list of the twelve division commanders to an end.

Did you know? In addition to the commanders of the military divisions, the chapter also lists officials over the tribes of Israel, including Eliezer over Reuben, Shephatiah over Simeon, and Zadok over Aaron.
Did you know? David did not count the Israelites who were twenty years old or younger, because the LORD had promised to multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.

Did you know? Joab son of Zeruiah began the census but did not complete it. According to the chapter, this brought wrath upon Israel, so the census results were not included in the records of King David's reign.
Did you know? The administration of the king's possessions covered many areas: treasuries, fields, vineyards, olive oil, cattle, camels, donkeys, and flocks. An official was appointed over each area.
Did you know? Jonathan, David's uncle, is described as a wise counselor and a scribe, while Jehiel son of Hachmoni served alongside the king's sons.

Did you know? Ahithophel was the king's counselor, and Hushai the Archite is described as the king's friend. At the end of the chapter, Jehoiada, Abiathar, and Joab are also mentioned in key leadership roles.
